key_insight: A 145,281-parameter multi-head quantum module replaced eight transformer blocks in a 30-billion-parameter LLM, displacing 16.33% of its parameters with limited accuracy loss.
engineering_relevance: Partitioning hidden states into small quantum heads enables NISQ-compatible integration into production-scale LLM architectures without encoding the full hidden width in one circuit.
method: Split 2,048 hidden dimensions into 32 heads using 8-qubit, 4-layer angle-encoded circuits.
Couple quantum heads through constrained classical linear mixers and learned readouts.
Train with exact statevector simulation, then execute quantum heads on a 156-qubit IBM Heron processor.
evidence_signal: Held-out perplexity ablations found mixers alone within 1–3% of the full module for fused spans, while a parameter-matched classical MLP remained a few percent ahead.
watch_item: Quantum advantage is unproven: limited-seed non-entangling and frozen-circuit controls beat the full module, and hardware execution does not establish end-to-end speedup.
paper_title: Multi-head Quantum Neural Networks: Replacing Transformer Blocks with NISQ Modules inside a 30-Billion-Parameter LLM
